title: With a 4x longer-lived kind-specific waste at the same reach, the waste vortices stop spreading in place and travel: the population's trait centroid moves 2.55 from the ancestor by t=10000 (twin 0.38; every standard-memory run <= 0.9) as a narrow cloud (R 0.4-0.6), with 7-22 new classes per 1000 t to the end (one seed)
summary: c58's trait3d world with the waste lifetime raised from 500 t to 2000 t (dw 0.002 -> 0.0005) and its diffusion lowered so that its reach sqrt(Dw/dw) stays 22 px (Dw 1 -> 0.25), seed 7 with mut_seed 7, T=10000, waste arm (sw 0.4) against the kind-blind twin with the same parameters and draws. Read with vnov.py (1000-t windows). The centroid's distance from the ancestor rises nearly steadily, 0.08, 0.24, 0.75, 1.02, 1.10, 1.26, 1.67, 2.16, 2.34, 2.55 (twin 0.04 -> 0.38); the cloud radius stays 0.4-0.6, so the population moves as one front instead of widening to radius ~1 and stopping as the standard-memory runs do (20261028T0006-c61-vortex-cloud-bounded). New classes per 1000 t 15,22,12,8,3,22,20,18,7,7 (twin 14,5,2,10,2,5,3,1,1,0); share of vortices on new ground (>0.4 from every trait seen before t-1000) peaks at 0.51 and 0.60 (twin <= 0.03); c30 significant new kinds with the diversity-corrected threshold 0,4,0,0,0,5,5,2,1 (twin 0,0,1,0,...), raw a* 0,1,0,0,0,1,1,1,1 (twin 0,1,0...). trait3c's own counts: classes held by >= 3 vortices 10/21/30/60 at t=1500/3000/4500/10000 (twin 7/12/17/20), first-time dominants after t=3000 8 (twin 2), 0 returns to an earlier dominant; heredity as before (160 trait jumps at mutations, 0 elsewhere). The maps (m7_spec_maps.png) show successive near-monomorphic sweeps.

finding.operator: kind-specific waste with a memory (lifetime 2000 t) longer than the population's trait turnover, reach held at 22 px
finding.world: collective/contrib/20261027T1401-c58-vortex-trait3d/world.py with WORLD_P {ew 0.25, sw 0.4, mut_dt 50, dw 0.0005, Dw 0.25}
finding.control: kind-blind twin (sw 0) with the same dw, Dw, seed and mutation draws
finding.result: centroid distance from ancestor at t~9300: 2.55 vs twin 0.38 (standard memory, seeds 3-5: 0.37-0.50 at the end, max 0.87); new classes per 1000 t in the last four windows 20,18,7,7 vs 3,1,1,0

limits: One seed, T=10000, 128^2; a second seed (10) is running. Two parameters changed together (dw and Dw) to keep the reach fixed; memory alone or reach alone were not separated. Mechanism, as I read world.py: the waste stores only the local MEAN trait of past eaters (V/W), and a vortex is held back by G = exp(-|theta - V/W|^2 / 2 sw^2); a long memory makes that mean lag behind the population, so the population is pushed away from its own recent past in a consistent direction, a self-repelling walk in trait space. The kinds still differ only in how the waste treats them (equal intrinsic fitness), so whether this escape is O or O by construction is the same open question as before (20261027T1800-c59-vortex-novelty-null). New ground arrives in bursts (sweeps), not at a steady rate.
